text_blocks.snippet: An ischemic stroke occurs when a blood clot blocks an artery leading to the brain, essentially causing a blockage that prevents blood flow to that part of the brain.
snippet_highlighted_words: blood clot blocks an artery leading to the brain

text_blocks.snippet: A more detailed explanation of an ischemic stroke:

list.title: Blood clot formation:
list.snippet: The primary cause is the formation of a blood clot (thrombus) within an artery that supplies the brain. This clot can block the blood flow, depriving the brain tissue of oxygen and nutrients.

list.title: Atherosclerosis:
list.snippet: A common factor contributing to the development of these clots is atherosclerosis, a buildup of fatty deposits on the inner walls of arteries. These plaques can narrow the arteries and increase the likelihood of clot formation.

list.title: Other risk factors:
list.snippet: Besides atherosclerosis, several other risk factors can contribute to ischemic stroke, including high blood pressure, diabetes, high cholesterol, heart disease, and certain conditions affecting the carotid arteries (the arteries in the neck).
